hints: Focus on free radical substitution, where each H in ethane can be replaced by Cl step by step all the way to full chlorination.
List the molecular formulae from one Cl to six Cls: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Cl}_2$ up to $\text{C}_2\text{Cl}_6$, then think about positional isomers for each.
Count 1,1- versus 1,2- type arrangements for the middle members and add them all up to get the total number of distinct C2 chloro-products.
walkthrough:
**Understand the reaction type**

Think of this as free radical substitution of an alkane. With excess chlorine and UV light, substitution keeps going until all H atoms are replaced.

General change:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 + n\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_{6-n}\text{Cl}_n + n\text{HCl}$$

**List all possible formulae**

We only count products that still have two carbons and at least one Cl. That gives six formulae, with $n = 1$ to $6$:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}, \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Cl}_2, \text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}_3, \text{C}_2\text{H}_2\text{Cl}_4, \text{C}_2\text{HCl}_5, \text{C}_2\text{Cl}_6$$

**Count structural isomers for each**

Now draw the different positions for the Cl atoms. Be friendly with 1,1- and 1,2- patterns.

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$: 1 isomer ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$)

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Cl}_2$: 2 isomers ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHCl}_2$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{ClCH}_2\text{Cl}$)

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}_3$: 2 isomers ($\text{CH}_3\text{CCl}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{ClCHCl}_2$)

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_2\text{Cl}_4$: 2 isomers ($\text{CH}_2\text{ClCCl}_3$ and $\text{CHCl}_2\text{CHCl}_2$)

$\text{C}_2\text{HCl}_5$: 1 isomer ($\text{CHCl}_2\text{CCl}_3$)

$\text{C}_2\text{Cl}_6$: 1 isomer ($\text{CCl}_3\text{CCl}_3$)

**Add them together**

Total distinct C2 products with Cl:
$$1 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 9$$

options.A: 6 is too low. It usually comes from counting only one isomer for each formula ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ to $\text{C}_2\text{Cl}_6$), so you miss the extra positional isomers for $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}_3$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2\text{Cl}_4$.
options.B: 7 is too low. It often means you spotted one extra isomer but missed the others, for example forgetting that both trichloroethane and tetrachloroethane each have two forms.
options.C: 8 is just one short. This is a classic miscount where one pair, often $\text{CH}_3\text{CCl}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{ClCHCl}_2$, or $\text{CH}_2\text{ClCCl}_3$ and $\text{CHCl}_2\text{CHCl}_2$, is counted as one product.
options.D: 9 is correct. The full list is 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 9 distinct two-carbon chlorinated products, from $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ all the way to $\text{CCl}_3\text{CCl}_3$.
